label: early original-phase 0/x/n/o-type token after a sequence starting with i/u/v/b/p/a
predicate: (phase == 0) & (t >= 1) & (t <= 3) & isin(in_tok, [tok("0"), tok("x"), tok("n"), tok("o"), tok("e"), tok("c"), tok("1"), tok("z")]) & isin(first_tok, [tok("i"), tok("u"), tok("v"), tok("b"), tok("p"), tok("a")])
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase at steps t=1-3 (99% of mass; t=2 alone holds 63%), never at t=0 and almost never in the delimiter/copy phases. The input token must come from a specific set: 0 and x are strongest, then n and o, then e, c, 1, z; it is almost always the first time that token appears. The preceding context sets how often and how strongly it fires: rates are highest when the sequence starts with i, u, v, b, p or a (and when those tokens sit two steps back). Top activations look like i i d [0] or i v q [n]. Without the context condition the token+position rule captures 97% of mass with only 15% precision. Adding the first-token condition raises precision to about 40%, with 51% recall and 72% mass recall on dev. That suggests a graded sum of token identity and early-prefix context rather than a crisp rule. Does not fire on letters like w, f, h, l, or on copy-phase outputs.
